relevance_note: Case report plus literature review of HA20, the disease caused by germline TNFAIP3 variants: the authors' own patient has a heterozygous TNFAIP3 frameshift variant ("Whole exome sequencing revealed a heterozygous mutation in the affected TNFAIP3 gene"), and Table 3 summarises 15 published paediatric HA20 cases.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema and the rules; no outside knowledge was used. All spans were copied from the Markdown and each was re-checked verbatim (the file uses U+00A0 and U+2005 spaces in places, reproduced as JSON escapes). Table 3 (15 literature cases, patients as rows) was transcribed cell by cell and checked against the table; its first column holds bare patient numbers, so labels follow the 'Table 3 #<value>' rule, and the parenthetical in that column (the source reference) was copied to source_reference_in_review. The Table 3 legend defines Y = yes and N = no, so N cells were recorded as 'excluded' with the legend quoted as a second span; the '—' (U+2014) and '−' (U+2212) cells in the 'Others' column were treated as not reported, and the treatment cells 'Without elaborating', '—' and '−' as 'not reported'. The Table 3 'Age (y)' column is age at diagnosis per its legend, so it was put in age_at_diagnosis_* and not in onset. No cell in this paper contained stacked values separated by ' / '. Checklist mapping of the free-text 'Others' column: 'Insulin-dependent diabetes'->type 1 diabetes, 'cytopenias'->cytopenia (autoimmune), 'hepatitis'->autoimmune hepatitis, 'enteropathy'->gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation, 'Hypothyroidism'/'Autoimmune thyroid disorder'->autoimmune thyroiditis, 'growth delay'->growth failure, 'Pericardial effusion'->pericarditis or other serositis, 'small vessel CNS vasculitis'->central nervous system involvement and vasculitis, 'lymphadenopathy'->lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy; the remaining 'Others' entries (pulmonary embolism, inflammatory fibroepithelial polyp, vomit, hepatic fibrosis, pharyngalgia, cow's milk allergy, Epstein-Barr virus infection) match no checklist item and appear only in phenotypic_features. Normal/negative findings were recorded as the abnormality they rule out (D-27): '| Bone marrow smear | Normal |' as 'abnormal bone marrow smear' (excluded), 'cerebrospinal fluid tests were negative' as 'abnormal cerebrospinal fluid tests' (excluded), the Table 1 'Negative' and 'Normal' cells as the corresponding positive/abnormal findings (excluded), and the whole-examination statement 'The rest of the cardiopulmonary, abdominal, joint, and neurological examination showed no significant abnormality' as excluded in the paper's own words, because a whole examination excludes nothing more specific than what it names, so the child's joint and other checklist items stay 'not reported'. The child is called 'the first witness' in the Figure 1 legend, a role word, so the case-report label 'patient' was used; the father, mother and grandparents are labelled by relation. The father carries the child's variant ('derived from the father'), so he has a variant row using the printed variant description; the mother and the grandparents have no variant rows, and the grandparents' negative test is reflected only in their individuals row. The child's thyroid antibody abnormality was not recorded as 'autoimmune thyroiditis' in the checklist because the paper does not diagnose thyroiditis. Inconsistencies found in the paper: the Discussion says 'IL-6, IL-4, and IL-10 all showed elevations' although Table 1 lists no IL-10; Table 1 prints 'CD3+ (620%–76.0%)', an evident typo; the admission examination says 'Oral mucosa was smooth' while later text reports recurrent oral ulcers (a time difference, not treated as a contradiction); 'The downstream truncation variant of this variant is known to be pathogenic.' is garbled but refers to this variant and was used for pathogenicity_as_stated_by_authors; publications.n_patients_reported = 16 (the 15 Table 3 patients plus the authors' own patient), while cohort_size_as_stated = 15, the total the authors state for their review.
